newsitem.title: UK: Boosey & Hawkes H1 results hit high note.
newsitem.headline: Boosey & Hawkes H1 results hit high note.

text.p: Boosey & Hawkes, the UK instrument maker and music publisher, said on Tuesday that gains across both its divisions had helped half-year profits hit a high note, rising 20.7 percent to a record 2.05 million stg.
Turnover rose to 42.1 million from 40.5 million, with margins and operating profits moving ahead.
Chief executive Richard Holland said he was confident of further progress by the year end.

The instrument division saw a sales rise thanks to fast growth in key markets in the Far East and the U.S. But some European markets, including France and Germany, were sluggish and Japan only showed a small recovery in volumes.
The unit's operating profit was up 18 percent to 1.52 million on turnover of 30.9 million, up 5.6 percent.
Its acquisition of Rico International, the manufacturer of reeds for clarinets and saxophones, was completed on August 30.
The publishing unit saw sales of printed music dampened by market weakness in several territories, but operating profits rose nine percent to 1.78 million even so.
This division's acquisition of Bote and Bock was completed in February and restructuring measures were taken in the first half.
